title: The great ones failed; the small ones set out
odia:
ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ ଗଲେ ଫସର ଫାଟି
ସାନ ବାହାରିଲେ ବେସର ବାଟି।
literal_meaning: The great ones came to nothing; the small ones set out, having ground mustard paste.
meaning_odia: ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ମାନେ ବିଫଳ ହୋଇଗଲେ, ଅଥଚ ସାନମାନେ ବେସର ବାଟି ବାହାରିଲେ—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର ପଙ୍କ୍ତିରେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆଗରୁ ଅଧିକ ସମର୍ଥ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଉଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ବିଫଳତା ଦେଖାଇ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରାଯାଉଛି। ବେସର କାହିଁକି ବଟା ହୋଇଛି ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ସାନ ବୋଲି କେହି ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ବିଫଳ ହେବେ ବୋଲି ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
explanation: The first line announces failure; the second shows others already equipped with a preparation of their own. Our editorial reading hears a sceptical challenge to their confidence: if the supposedly greater people failed, what makes these smaller ones so ready? The question can discourage ambition, but the verse supplies no outcome for the later attempt.
usage_example: Original imagined example: After experienced teams abandon a difficult task, newcomers announce that they are ready. Someone quotes the mustard-paste line sceptically; the newcomers still have to show what their different approach can achieve.
cultural_context: Grinding mustard paste gives readiness a tangible action. The saying leaves its intended use unexplained, so the translation preserves the preparation without supplying a dish, a catch or a missing story.

english_summary: Earlier failure is set against the readiness of those considered smaller.
